<!-- pr-reviewer: 31130d669c5ddf2e5e68213798c2f7340e5e9903 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes toolpath geometry: Rotary Parallel now clips its cut to the picked faces.

### What looks good

- The clip plans no new motion. Each kept point is a point that the whole-model raster already passed through the gouge laws. The axis fit, the gouge laws and the verify still read the full model.
- Between two kept pieces, the clip puts a `Plunge` marker. `rotary_links` reads `Rapid | Plunge` as a link (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_links.rs:110`), so the relink lifts the tool to the retract cylinder. The tool does not feed straight across the part that was left out. This is the same pattern as `rotary_ends::clip`.
- The facet indices are correct. `named_material` reads `setup_align::facets_in` in model order and drops no facet (`crates/app/src/operation/material.rs:230-255`). So the index of a face facet names the same facet in `material.facets`.
- Each unusable selection refuses by name. Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset refuse a face selection. Before this PR, they cut the full model and gave no message.
- There are two layers of protection. With the `faces_outward` guard off (mutation M2), the kernel still refuses an end-cap pick with "no pass lies over the picked faces".
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in non-test code. The float-to-index casts saturate and clamp. The new files have provenance lines and are less than 400 lines. The decision record is in `docs/decisions/2848-rotary-face-selection.md`. No new crate dependency.
- No golden moved (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `tests/golden`). No UI code, so no screenshots are necessary.

### Results merged with main (locally)

The trial merge of the PR head with `upstream/main` is clean. All tests ran locally on macOS, debug, with the compile cache off. The sccache server of this machine does not answer.

The quick-gate plan (`--dry-run`) mapped 962 steps. It compared against the PR's old base, so it included all of the newer main. I ran the suites that cover the touched code:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app `rotary_face_selection` (new pins) | 5 passed |
| app `rotary_verify` | 9 passed |
| app `rotary_letter` | 3 passed |
| app `rotary_fixtures` | 4 passed |
| app `rotary_feed_cap` | 11 passed |
| app `rotary_field_parity` | 3 passed, 6 ignored (heavy lane) |
| app `center_cut_multiaxis` | 6 passed |
| app `mcp_rotary_stack` | 1 passed |
| app `stock_stamp` | 4 passed |
| app `setup_align_multiaxis` | 10 passed |
| motion lib `multiaxis::` (includes 3 `rotary_pick` unit tests) | 72 passed |
| motion `multiaxis`, `rotary`, `rotary_links`, `rotary_offset` | 7, 11, 7, 9 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Mutations (re-run by the reviewer)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| M1: the kernel clip off (`match picked` reads `None`) | 3 keep pins red |
| M2: the `faces_outward` guard off | refusal pin red |
| M3: no `Plunge` marker between kept pieces | clip unit test red; `rotary_parallel_keeps_its_cut_over_the_picked_faces` red |

After each mutation, I put the code back. The pins are green again.

### Extra suites run

- Test data: the PR changes no file under `testdata/` and no fixture directory. Not applicable.
- Importers: the PR does not touch the import code or `crates/kernel`. Not applicable.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_pick.rs:398-412` (`Shadow::holds`): the ray from the axis has no length limit. A pick that also has facets at a smaller radius (for example a patch that includes a bore wall) can keep cut points over the outer surface above that wall. This changes only the extent of the cut, not its safety, because each kept point is certified on the full model. A follow-up can limit the ray to the ball centre's radius if necessary.
2. `faces_outward` passes a pick if one facet looks away from the axis (`any`). A mixed patch passes the guard. The note above applies.
3. `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs` has 503 lines (+3 in this PR). It was more than 400 lines before this PR.
4. The PR body says the issue can stay open until #2851 and #2852 merge. The maintainer decides `Fixes` or `Refs`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 31130d669c5ddf2e5e68213798c2f7340e5e9903 -->
Read-only second review (Opus). Not built here.

Verdict: Ready to merge.

Safety-floor second read of the full diff at head 31130d669. This review did not build, test or change the PR. It read the diff, the touched files at the head, `material.rs`, `stamp.rs` and `rotary_links.rs`.

## Blockers

None.

## What this review checked

1. **No silent ignore is left on a rotary kind.** `rotary_picks::picks_of` returns a value for each `SrcRef::Selection` on the three rotary kinds. Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset get a named refusal (`not_yet`). The Contour/Parallel arm calls `usable` before the kernel. The Offset arm reads `rotary_picks.take()` and returns the error. These cases refuse by name:
   - an empty selection;
   - an edge chain or a vertex pick;
   - picks on two models, and a model that is gone;
   - a face id or patch id that is no longer in the features (stale pick);
   - a facet index out of range of the material;
   - a face that does not look away from the axis (an end cap, a bore wall);
   - picks in two or more groups;
   - picks that no pass lies over (`GenError::Empty`).
   I found no path in `generate.rs` that calls a rotary kernel without this check. `guard_posed` calls the same `run` closure.
2. **No selection gives the old path.** `rotary_parallel_in` calls `rotary_parallel_over(.., None, ..)`, and `None => base` is the old code. No `.nc` or `.cl` golden moved. There is no explicit equality pin, but the code path is the same and the existing rotary suites passed in the first review.
3. **The region on the cylinder.** The shadow test is a 3D ray from the axis line through the ball centre (Moller-Trumbore). It uses no angle parameter, so there is no wrap at 0/360 degrees, and a face that crosses the seam has no special case. The laid frame has its origin on the fitted axis and local x along it (`rotary.rs`), so the ray origin `(c.x, 0, 0)` is on the axis.
4. **Gouge and links.** The clip keeps only points of the whole-model raster, which the gouge laws certified against all facets. Between two kept pieces it puts a `Plunge` marker. `rotary_links` reads `Rapid | Plunge` as a link, so the relink goes out to the retract cylinder and does not feed across the left-out stretch. The verify still runs on the result, and a blocking warning still blocks the post (the pins assert no `blocks_post` warning).
5. **Facet indices.** `named_material` reads `setup_align::facets_in` in model order and drops no facet. `usable` in `material.rs` only refuses non-finite input; it does not filter. So the facet index of a face names the same facet in `material.facets`. This agrees with the first review.
6. **Stamp.** The `SrcRef::Selection` arm of `current_stamp` already digests each pick (kind, entity, id) and the pose and geometry signature of each picked model. A change of selection therefore makes the cache stale, before and after this PR. The new `rotary-picked-faces-v1` mark makes old caches of a rotary operation with a selection read stale one time. An old project loads, reads Stale, and the post refuses it until a regenerate. That is the correct result.
7. **Float and index math.** `holds` refuses a centre with `rho <= 1e-9` or non-finite. `ray_meets` refuses a near-zero determinant, scaled to the edge lengths. `faces_outward` refuses zero-length normals and radials. The bin index is clamped. `spans` caps its samples at 2^20 for each chord, and the bisection has 40 rounds. `groups` indexes only inside `0..facets.len()`. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests.
8. **Code shape and layers.** `generate.rs` gets about 10 lines: one call in each arm and no new logic. The world reads are in `crates/app/src/operation/rotary_picks.rs` (122 lines, reads the ECS world: correct crate). The clip is in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_pick.rs` (344 lines, domain values only: correct crate). `rotary.rs` goes to 364 lines. `job.rs` was over 400 lines before (+3). No new crate dependency. Each new file has a provenance line.
9. **Tests.** `crates/app/tests/rotary_face_selection.rs` imports `camcraft_app` items and has its Gate map line. The pins assert the station of each feed and plunge end, and of each move on the neck pick, not only "it generates". The sector pin asserts the angle range and the radial pose about the axis of the whole bar. The refusal pins cover disconnected picks, an end cap, an end cap mixed with good faces, an edge chain, and the Contour and Offset refusals. The Contour and Offset pin also generates the whole model again as a control. No existing test is changed or made weaker.
10. **Records.** `docs/decisions/2848-rotary-face-selection.md` is present. The body has a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2848`.

## Gate evidence on this head (from the PR text)

- The author ran `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on this head: green, 294 steps, 0 failed. The author ran clippy on `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-app` with `-D warnings`: clean.
- The first review (the session of mkinney) ran the touched rotary and multiaxis suites, the motion lib `multiaxis::` tests and clippy on a trial merge, macOS debug: all green. It also ran three mutations.
- No batch tier and no release tier ran on this head. The heavy lane was not run: `rotary_field_parity` reports 6 ignored tests.
- The quick gate compared against an older main (base 326c938b1). `origin/main` is now at e47dc1042.

## Trial merge

`git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/pr-2853` with `origin/main` at e47dc1042: clean, no conflict.

## Notes (not blocking)

1. `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_pick.rs:396-412` (`Shadow::holds`): the ray has no length limit. A pick with facets at a larger or smaller radius on the same radial can keep a point over an unpicked face. This changes only the extent of the cut. Each kept point stays certified on the full model, so the tool does not go below the model surface. The first review gave the same note.
2. The clip contains the ball centre, not the ball. Near the edge of a pick, the ball touches the next unpicked face up to the tool radius, on the model surface. This is the usual meaning of tool containment. The decision file or the UI text can say it.
3. `groups` welds vertices at 1e-6 mm by rounding. Two vertices that are equal to within float noise but fall on two sides of a rounding step give a false "not connected" refusal. This fails safe (a refusal, not a wrong cut). Shared vertices of one mesh are normally bit-equal.
4. A face with no facets gets the "does not face away from the work axis" message. The refusal is correct, but the words do not match the cause.
5. Cost: for a large pick whose facets cover the full length, each bin holds all facets, and each 0.25 mm sample tests each of them. The time is bounded but can be long. The PR body says that this was not measured.
6. No pin covers the `rotary-picked-faces-v1` mark. If a later change removes it, an old cached whole-model path of a rotary selection reads fresh again. Consider a test that asserts the stamp of a rotary selection is different from the same operation with a non-rotary kind, or a comment at the mark that names this PR.
7. The "Done means" list of the issue asks for containment on all three rotary kinds. This PR does it for Rotary Parallel and makes the other two refuse. #2851 and #2852 are open and hold the remaining work. With the closing keyword in the body, the issue closes at merge. The maintainer decides if `Refs` is better. The silent-ignore defect is removed for all three kinds, so the closing keyword is acceptable.
8. Not exercised by any test: a WCS yaw or a part alignment with a face selection, and the ramped infeed on clipped passes. The PR body lists these.
